title: unified-constraint-adapter-and-token-boundary-polish
author: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Multiple constrained-decoding backends (CFG/grammar, regex, and the legacy token-mask backend) behave inconsistently in two problem areas: 1) the adapter layer that translates a top-level constraint spec into backend-specific inputs had divergent semantics (e.g. inclusive vs exclusive anchors), which caused structured-output regressions when falling back between backends; 2) tokenizer edge-cases—multibyte tokens, surrogate pairs, and custom tokenizer merges—were producing partial-token cutoffs when streaming and when performing function/tool call framing, leading to invalid JSON or truncated tool arguments in some streams.

What this PR does: Adds a unified ConstraintAdapter that normalizes high-level constraint specs into a canonical intermediate representation and then emits backend-specific payloads (CFG, regex, token-mask). It also introduces a TokenBoundaryPolisher that post-processes streaming token chunks to avoid emitting partial tokens and to maintain deterministic cursor positions for the KV cache. The adapter is intentionally conservative to preserve semantics when falling back between backends and when using openai-compat streaming.

Key design points (summary):
- Canonical intermediate model: a small, well-documented IR (ConstraintIR) that represents sequences, alternations, optional groups, and anchors. This IR is plain data (no engine code) and is the single source of truth for translation rules.
- Backend translators: thin, fully-tested translators for CFG, regex, and token-mask. Each translator preserves optional group semantics and emits explicit token-boundary hints where possible.
- TokenBoundaryPolisher: during streaming we buffer up to N bytes (configurable, default 32) to detect incomplete token boundaries (multibyte or merged tokens) and only forward full tokens to the stream sink. This reduces latency by average 3% for long sequences while eliminating malformed JSON/tool-call edgecases.
- OpenAI-compat framing: the adapter respects function/tool calling framing rules and reframes constraint payloads to ensure deterministic framing in the OpenAI-compat stream shim. This fixes cases where tools were receiving truncated args in compatibility mode.
- Backward compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior; a feature-flag
--enable-canonical-constraints (off in stable) gates the new adapter. Rollout plan uses a gradual flag ramp to Dedicated tenants before enabling globally.

Checklist:
- [x] Add ConstraintIR and translators (CFG/regex/token-mask)
- [x] Implement TokenBoundaryPolisher and integrate with streaming layer
- [x] Add unit tests for tokenizer edge cases (emoji, surrogates, BPE merges)
- [x] Add integration tests for OpenAI-compat tool framing with fallbacks
- [x] Update docs and SDK contract notes (docstrings + short changelog entry)

Testing notes and results:
- Unit test bundle added: runtime/tests/test_constraint_adapter.py (60 cases) and tokenizer/tests/test_boundary_polisher.py (48 edge cases).
- Integration: ran openai-compat integration pipeline against sample tool-calling harness. First CI run surfaced a flaky streaming test due to an unrelated socket timeout; fixed by adding better drain logic in stream_sink. Final CI: all green.
- Performance: microbenchmarks on a p3.2xlarge-like shape show median additional CPU cost of ~0.6% for constraint translation and an average 3% token throughput improvement in stable streaming due to reduced reassembly work downstream.

Migration / rollout:
- The change is behind --enable-canonical-constraints; will be enabled only for 3 internal Dedicated tenants for two weeks, then rolled to beta customers, and then to default-on. We added a telemetry flag to record fallsbacks and any serialization errors to monitor regressions.

Files changed (high-level): see changed_files list.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to tokenizer boundary heuristics (tokenizer/token_boundary.pyi and tokenizer/boundary_polisher.cc) and to the translator unit tests which include aggressive negative cases. The ConstraintIR is intentionally tiny to keep the attack surface small.

Release notes:
- Add canonical constraint adapter and streaming token boundary fixes to improve structured-output stability and OpenAI-compat tool calling. Feature-gated rollout.
